tb21_profile.skill: Crack a password-protected 7z archive: extract the archive hash (7z2john), run a dictionary/brute-force attack (john/hashcat + wordlist), then extract secret_file.txt with the recovered password
tb21_profile.domain: Offensive-security tooling / cryptography: password & hash cracking, archive formats (7-zip, zip), rockyou-style wordlists
tb21_profile.task_form: reverse-engineer/crack a secret to recover data — find-the-password then extract, single answer written to a file

verifier_notes: security_20260420_020307_002 (OpenSSL AES cred-cracking, an ideal skill match) is graded FREE — its 2 tests only check solution.txt looks right — so it is deliberately kept out and not even shortlisted. security_20260610_111702_002 (GPG passphrase recovery) is also FREE and stays in CalibForge per_source only. RTS crackme family is all 'absent' (no verifier in our copy); I keep the closest ones in final_top10 as the spec allows, but note the verification gap. TMax zip/hash-crack tasks graded 'ok'/'strong' do pin the recovered password in a test, which is the load-bearing check here.
searches: tools.py words tmax password crack archive zip encrypted recover secret decrypt hash extract

notes: TMax-15K is clearly the strongest pool for this task and dominates the top of final_top10: it has genuine zip/PIN password-cracking and hash-cracking-with-rockyou tasks that transfer almost one-to-one, with pinned-value verifiers. CalibForge is a close second and contributes three verified crack/decrypt-to-solution.txt tasks (the exact output path), so the two new corpora DO beat the old ones in one place — CalibForge's security_* set outranks everything from TerminalWorld/RTS/SWE except TMax. Terminal-Lego's contribution is real but weaker: it teaches the hash-cracking/archive domain via 'demonstrate/implement' exercises rather than an actual crack, so its best (task_01697, a wordlist MD5 cracker fix) is a 4 at most. RTS has no verifier (all absent) but its crackme family is the honest closest match there; I placed one in final_top10 per the spec and flagged the gap. SWE-Smith and SWE-Rebench have essentially nothing on password cracking — their best entries are secrets-manager/archive-handling library fixes that top out at overall 2; both corpora should be treated as filler here. No FREE candidate appears in final_top10 (security_20260420_020307_002 and security_20260610_111702_002, both ideal-looking but FREE, are excluded).
